title: Projective bundles of arbitrary quasi-coherent modules classify invertible quotients
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal E$ any quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_S$-module [pqf-def-coherent], without a finite-type or local-freeness hypothesis. Put $P=\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}\mathcal E)$ and $p:P\to S$, using the canonical symmetric graded algebra [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra] and relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj]. The affine degree-one twisting modules [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] glue canonically to an invertible module $\mathcal O_P(1)$ [def-sc-invertible-module]. The degree-one maps give a canonical surjection $p^*\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O_P(1)$, with pullback as in [def-pc-module-pullback]. For every scheme morphism $h:T\to S$, pullback of this quotient is a bijection between $S$-morphisms $a:T\to P$ and isomorphism classes of pairs $(\mathcal L,q)$ with $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_T$-module and $q:h^*\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal L$ a surjective sheaf homomorphism. Here $(\mathcal L,q)$ and $(\mathcal L',q')$ are isomorphic exactly when an isomorphism $v:\mathcal L\to\mathcal L'$ satisfies $v q=q'$. The bijection is natural under arbitrary pullback $T'\to T$; the morphism attached to $q$ has a quotient-compatible isomorphism $a^*\mathcal O_P(1)\cong\mathcal L$, and equals the canonical relative-Proj morphism of the induced graded map $h^*\operatorname{Sym}\mathcal E\to\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map]. For any open $V\subseteq S$, $P\times_S V$ with its quotient and twist identifies canonically with $\mathbf P_V(\mathcal E|_V)$ with its quotient and twist. The map $p$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]. For $\mathcal E=\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(r+1)}$, $r\ge0$, this identifies $(P,\mathcal O_P(1))$ with $(\mathbf P^r_S,\mathcal O(1))$ [def-nagata-relative-projective-space, def-pc-projective-space-twist]; over $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ this is $(\operatorname{Proj}A[T_0,\ldots,T_r],\widetilde{A[T_0,\ldots,T_r](1)})$.

source.place: Tag 01OB (definition-projective-bundle) and the subsequent quotient-functor discussion in Section 01OA (section-projective-bundle); Tag 01O4 (lemma-apply-relative), Tag 01O9 (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), Tag 01OD (lemma-projective-bundle-separated), and Tag 01OE (lemma-projective-space-bundle).

proof.text: Work over an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq S$ and put $M=\mathcal E(U)$, $A=\operatorname{Sym}_R M$. The canonical graded algebra [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra] has degree-$d$ part spanned by products of $d$ elements of $M$. Thus the images $e=\iota(m)$, for all $m\in M$, generate $A_+$ as an ideal. By [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists], $p^{-1}U=\operatorname{Proj}A$; by [prop-nagata-proj-standard-open], its opens $D_+(e)=\operatorname{Spec}H_e$, $H_e=(A_e)_0$, cover it. On base overlaps choose affine refinements using [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. All subsequent comparisons use the restriction maps of this canonical algebra and the compatible affine identifications in the relative-Proj existence statement.

On $D_+(e)$ the affine twist [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] is $(A_e)_1$. Multiplication by $e$ identifies it with $H_e$: its inverse sends $a/e^k$ of degree one to $a/e^{k+1}$ of degree zero. The composites are identities in the localized ring, including when a chart is empty. On $D_+(e)\cap D_+(f)$ its generators satisfy $e=(e/f)f$, with $e/f$ a unit; this overlap is $D(f/e)$ inside the $e$ chart by [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection]. These identifications are the restriction maps of the affine twisting module, since both act on homogeneous fractions. On changing the base affine, the coefficient restriction sends $a/e^k$ to $\overline a/\overline e^k$, and sends the frame $e$ to $\overline e$. Hence the local free modules and their inverses agree under base restriction, by the canonical-algebra restriction data of [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra]. Their cocycle on every triple overlap is $(e/f)(f/g)=e/g$. Glue them by [lem-weil-pbc-site-module-sheaf-gluing] on the Zariski open site of $P$. This gives exactly the specified affine twists, a global module $\mathcal O_P(1)$ locally free of rank one, hence invertible by [def-sc-invertible-module].

The section $m\in M$ maps on each chart to $\iota(m)/1\in(A_e)_1$, the degree-one section map of [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf]. These maps respect localization and restriction on the base, so define $\mathcal E\to p_*\mathcal O_P(1)$. Adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] gives $q_P:p^*\mathcal E\to\mathcal O_P(1)$. On $D_+(e)$, it sends the pulled-back $m$ with $\iota(m)=e$ to the frame $e$ of Step 2. It is therefore surjective on that chart, hence on their cover and thus globally. For an arbitrary $a:T\to P$ over $S$, tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] takes a local frame to a local frame. Pulling back these local surjections consequently gives a surjection $h^*\mathcal E\to a^*\mathcal O_P(1)$ onto an invertible module.

source.place: Tag 01OA (section-projective-bundle), canonical maps immediately after Definition 01OB

proof.text: Conversely, let $q:h^*\mathcal E\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal L$ be a quotient in the statement. Adjunction [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] gives $\mathcal E\to h_*\mathcal L$. Include this into the degree-one summand of the commutative algebra $h_*(\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\mathcal L^{\otimes d})$. The universal property [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra] extends it uniquely to an algebra map from $\operatorname{Sym}\mathcal E$. It preserves degrees: a product of $d$ generators goes to the tensor product of their $d$ images; these span the degree-$d$ piece by [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra]. Adjunction, degree by degree, gives the induced graded map $\psi:h^*\operatorname{Sym}\mathcal E\to\bigoplus_{d\ge0}\mathcal L^{\otimes d}$ with $\psi_1=q$. Since $q$ is surjective, $U(\psi)=T$. The scheme case of [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map] therefore gives its canonical $S$-morphism $r:T\to P$. The next steps check its quotient and the inverse property explicitly, rather than presuming either from that node.

Here is an explicit construction from $q$ that will identify $r$ without using any unrecorded property of that morphism. Choose $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$ and an affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset h^{-1}U$ trivializing $\mathcal L$, with frame $l$; such $W$ cover $T$ by [def-sc-invertible-module] and [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-affine-sections], $(h^*\mathcal E)(W)=M\otimes_R B$. The same affine-sections formula on principal affine neighborhoods shows that the $m\otimes1$ generate the source stalks. Write $q(m\otimes1)=b_m l$. The principal opens $W_m=D(b_m)$ cover $W$: surjectivity says that the $b_m$ generate the unit ideal in every stalk, and if all lay in the maximal ideal of a stalk they could not generate $1$. For $e=\iota(m)$, write $b(a)\in B$ for the coefficient of $l^{\otimes d}$ in $\psi(a)$, $a\in A_d$. The formula $a/e^d\mapsto b(a)/b_m^d$ defines an $R$-algebra map $H_e\to B[1/b_m]$. It is well defined: apply the algebra map $A\to B$, $\iota(v)\mapsto b_v$, to a localization relation and invert $b_m$. Addition and multiplication of fractions are respected. The affine-spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives a morphism $W_m\to D_+(e)\subset P$ over $S$.

source.place: Tag 01O4 via the affine construction of Tag 01NA (lemma-apply); homogeneous-fraction formulas in 01O9

proof.text: The maps of Step 5 glue. Indeed, on $W_m\cap W_n$ the fraction $f/e$, with $f=\iota(n)$, maps to $b_n/b_m$, a unit. By [lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection], the two maps land in $D_+(e)\cap D_+(f)$. Their homomorphisms agree there: a degree-zero homogeneous fraction maps in either case to its value under $b$, with the denominator inverted. Changing the frame to $l'=u l$ replaces the coefficient $b(a)$ of degree $d$ by $u^{-d}b(a)$, so leaves $b(a)/b_m^d$ unchanged. On an affine refinement of two base opens, coefficient restriction gives exactly the same formula, using the canonical restrictions of [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra] and the target identifications of [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] yields a morphism $a_q:T\to P$, independent of all choices. These are precisely the homogeneous-fraction formulas for the usual canonical morphism from a graded map into powers of an invertible module. Since the scheme clause of [lem-trf-space-line-module-proj-map] identifies its morphism with that usual construction, $a_q=r_{\mathcal L,\psi}$.

source.place: Tags 01O4 and 01O9, affine-chart construction and its gluing; quotient discussion in 01OA

proof.text: On $W_m$, the line $a_q^*\mathcal O_P(1)$ has the frame pulled back from $e$ on $D_+(e)$. Send that frame to $q(m)=b_m l$, which is a frame of $\mathcal L$ there. This is an isomorphism of free rank-one modules. It carries $a_q^*q_P(v)$ to $q(v)$ for every local section $v$: in the $e$ frame the former has coefficient $\iota(v)/e$, which pulls back to $b_v/b_m$, and multiplying this by $b_m l$ gives $b_v l$. On an overlap with the $f$ frame, the transition $e=(e/f)f$ pulls back to $b_m l=(b_m/b_n)b_n l$. Hence these isomorphisms agree and glue, along with their inverses, by the sheaf axiom. The same equality covers changes of frame and base. We obtain a quotient-compatible isomorphism $a_q^*\mathcal O_P(1)\cong\mathcal L$, using tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] and the homogeneous-fraction description [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf].

source.place: Tag 01OA, inverse quotient constructions; degree-one part of theta in Tag 01O9

proof.text: Start now with any $S$-morphism $a:T\to P$ and pull back $q_P$. On the inverse image of each degree-one chart $D_+(e)$ over an affine base, use the pulled-back $e$ as frame. The quotient coefficients are $a^*(v/e)$; in particular the coefficient of $e$ is $1$. The construction of Steps 5--6 therefore recovers the restriction of $a$, since its map on every homogeneous fraction $c/e^d$ is $a^*(c/e^d)$: express $c$ as a sum of products of $d$ degree-one elements using [def-trf-canonical-symmetric-graded-algebra]. On affine refinements equality of these ring maps gives equality of scheme maps by [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] gives equality globally. In the other direction Step 7 recovers the quotient pair up to exactly the required compatible isomorphism. If $v:\mathcal L\simeq\mathcal L'$ carries $q$ to $q'$, choose the frame $v(l)$ for $\mathcal L'$; all coefficients $b_m$ agree, so their constructed maps agree. Thus the two constructions descend to isomorphism classes and are inverse bijections.

source.place: Tag 01OA, inverse bijections, expanding the appeal to 01O4

proof.text: For $u:T'\to T$, tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback] carries each quotient frame $q(m)$ on $W_m$ to a quotient frame on $u^{-1}W_m$. Its coefficient map sends $b(a)/b_m^d$ to $u^*b(a)/(u^*b_m)^d$. This is also the composite chart map for $a_q\circ u$. Affine refinements and uniqueness of scheme gluing [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-morphism-gluing] give $a_{u^*q}=a_q\circ u$; the isomorphisms of Step 7 agree because both send the pulled-back frame $e$ to $u^*q(m)$. No flatness is used: pulling back a locally invertible frame preserves it. For an open $V\subset S$, [lemma-nagata-relative-proj-exists] identifies the restrictions of $P$ and $\mathbf P_V(\mathcal E|_V)$ on every affine open of $V$, compatibly on further restriction and with the base maps. These identify the schemes over $V$; restriction to $V$ is the fibre product with the open subscheme by the universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. The fraction description in [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf] identifies their twists and their degree-one quotient maps. Thus the claimed open-base identification respects both the quotient and the twist.

source.place: Tag 01OA, functoriality of the quotient construction; Tags 01NQ and 01NR, restriction and twist gluing

proof.text: The separatedness theorem [lem-trf-projective-bundle-separated] applies to the present quasi-coherent $\mathcal E$: its statement requires neither finite type nor local freeness. It gives that $p:\operatorname{Proj}_S(\operatorname{Sym}\mathcal E)\to S$ is separated. This is the same structural morphism as in Step 1, with the canonical symmetric grading.

Finally take $\mathcal E=\mathcal O_S^{\oplus(r+1)}$ with its standard basis. The definition [def-nagata-relative-projective-space] uses precisely the symmetric algebra and symmetric grading of this free module for $\mathbf P^r_S$; on an affine base it is the standard graded polynomial algebra $A[T_0,\ldots,T_r]$. Thus its relative Proj is $P$, with the same standard charts. Step 2 makes the twist free on the chart $D_+(T_i)$ with frame $T_i$, satisfying $T_i=(T_i/T_j)T_j$. These are the transition rules of [def-pc-projective-space-twist], so the frame-preserving maps and their inverses glue to identify the twists. By [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], over $\operatorname{Spec}A$ the resulting module is exactly $\widetilde{A[T_0,\ldots,T_r](1)}$. This proves all the asserted projective-space identifications, including $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 01OE (lemma-projective-space-bundle), with Definition 01OB and the standard degree-one twist

proof_origin.place: Tags 01OA/01OB, quotient-functor discussion; 01O4 and its affine degree-one localization argument; 01O9; 01OD; 01OE. Chart calculations and gluing are written out.
